correctness.rationale: The standard Rudin–Shapiro doubling identities yield a four-state 2-morphism. Its complete eight adjacent-state-pair closure enumerates all length-eight factors by starting parity, and a reproducible exact test establishes the two disjoint sets (24 even, 32 odd). This forces equal long factors to start with the same parity. Decimation of equal even- or odd-start factors produces equal half-length factors; base values at lengths 1–10 are enumerated. Induction for every n>=11 proves the lower first-collision bound 2R(ceil(n/2)) and constructs the unique previous match at zero using the even recurrence. The exact closed formula and liminf/limsup follow. The verifier compares a morphic generator to independent binary arithmetic on 131072 positions and exhaustively checks first collisions for lengths 1–1024 and nine larger cases. The finite checks corroborate but do not replace infinite induction.

value.rationale: Exact all-length solution for the established initial non-repetitive complexity invariant of a classical 2-automatic word, beyond finite census. Sharp power-of-two jump law, unique matching position, and normalized limit inferior two/limit superior four are useful structural information for comparing prefix repetition across automatic words. The phase-recognition lemma explains the phenomenon and the theorem is not a standard abelian-complexity corollary.
